discoveryHook.scenario: When you try on a shirt, the difference between your actual size and the shirt's size is like a residual. The smaller the difference, the better the fit. In math, residuals tell us how well a line of fit models the data — small, randomly scattered residuals mean a great fit!

explanation: A [[kw:residual]] is the difference between the observed $ y $-value and the $ y $-value predicted by the line of fit.
Residual = actual $ y $ − model $ y $. Positive if the data point is above the line, negative if below.
To assess the fit, calculate residuals for all data points and plot them against $ x $. This is a [[imp:residual plot]].
If residuals are randomly scattered around the horizontal axis with no pattern, the model is a [[imp:good fit]].
If residuals show a pattern (like a U‑shape or curve), the data may not be linear, and the model is not appropriate.

discoveryHook.scenario: A line of best fit is the most precise line possible — it minimizes the sum of the squared residuals, like a perfectly tailored suit. Graphing calculators and spreadsheets use linear regression to find this line instantly, giving you the equation and a correlation coefficient $ r $ that tells you how strong the fit is.

explanation: [[kw:Linear regression]] is a method that finds the precise line of best fit for a data set by using all data points.
The equation is given as $ y = ax + b $ (or $ y = mx + b $), where $ a $ is the slope and $ b $ is the $ y $-intercept.
The [[kw:correlation coefficient]] $ r $ measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship. Its values range from $ -1 $ to $ 1 $.
$ r $ close to $ 1 $ → strong [[imp:positive correlation]]. $ r $ close to $ -1 $ → strong [[imp:negative correlation]]. $ r $ close to $ 0 $ → weak or no correlation.
Technology also gives $ r^2 $, the coefficient of determination, but $ r $ is most commonly used to describe correlation.

notes: $ r > 0 $ means positive slope; $ r < 0 $ means negative slope.

rows.2: Time until next eruption increases by about 12 minutes for each additional minute of duration.

explanation: The [[imp:slope]] of the line of best fit is the rate of change of $ y $ with respect to $ x $. It answers: 'For each unit increase in $ x $, how much does $ y $ change on average?'
The [[imp:y-intercept]] is the predicted value of $ y $ when $ x = 0 $. It is the starting point of the linear model.
Interpretation must be in the context of the data. If $ x = 0 $ is outside the range of the data (as it often is), the $ y $-intercept may not have a meaningful real‑world interpretation.
Always check whether the slope and intercept make sense in the given situation.

confusionCorner.body: Extrapolation assumes the trend continues unchanged outside the observed range. In reality, trends can level off, reverse, or change. Always mention that extrapolated predictions are speculative.

formulaCard.title: Interpolation vs. Extrapolation
notes: Extrapolation should be used with caution.
formulaCard.formula: $$ \text{Interpolation: within data range; Extrapolation: beyond data range} $$

rows.0: Duration for a wait of 77 min?

explanation: [[kw:Interpolation]] uses a model to estimate a value [[imp:within]] the range of the given $ x $-values. It is generally reliable if the model is a good fit.
[[kw:Extrapolation]] uses a model to predict a value [[imp:outside]] the range of the given $ x $-values. It is less reliable, especially far outside the data range.
To interpolate or extrapolate, substitute the $ x $-value into the regression equation and solve for $ y $, or vice versa.
Always note whether your prediction is an interpolation or an extrapolation and be cautious with extrapolated values.

discoveryHook.scenario: Guessing a friend's height based on their age is easier if they're 10 and you know the heights of 9- and 11-year-olds (interpolation). Guessing the height of a 30-year-old from that same data is much riskier (extrapolation). The further you go outside known data, the less certain your prediction.

teacherCues: Plot Old Faithful data points. Mark a point between known x-values and ask: 'Is it safer to predict here or far to the right beyond the data?'
Define interpolation as predicting between known points, extrapolation as predicting beyond.

blocks.title: Blueprint Aid – Correlation, Causation, and the Full Analysis

discoveryHook.scenario: Just because two things happen together doesn't mean one causes the other — like ice cream sales and sunburns both rise in summer, but ice cream doesn't cause sunburns. This is the crucial difference between correlation and causation. The blueprint will guide you through a full data analysis: assess fit, find the model, and draw careful conclusions.

explanation: [[kw:Causation]] means a change in one variable [[imp:directly causes]] a change in another. Correlation alone does not imply causation.
A strong correlation may exist without causation (e.g., number of firefighters and fire damage — more firefighters at larger fires).

The blueprint for analyzing lines of fit: [[imp:Understand]] — plot data, check correlation (positive/negative/none). [[imp:Solve]] — use technology to find the line of best fit and correlation coefficient; calculate residuals to assess fit. [[imp:Conclude]] — interpret slope and intercept; make predictions via interpolation/extrapolation; discuss possible causation versus mere correlation.

notes: Always check residuals or $ r $ before trusting the model.
State whether a prediction is interpolation or extrapolation.

title: Chapter 4.5 — Analyzing Lines of Fit
presenterNotes: Residuals are the key diagnostic tool. Emphasize that a random scatter of residuals supports a linear model, while a pattern suggests a different type of relationship.
When using technology, walk through the exact steps on a calculator. Many students struggle with entering lists and finding LinReg.
The distinction between correlation and causation is critical for statistical literacy. Use multiple real-world examples to drive the point home.
The blueprint pulls together the entire chapter: writing equations, interpreting slope/intercept, using technology, and drawing appropriate conclusions.
